summary: New sense 1: trans. durch Einkochen vermindern, konzentrieren (mit ʕal-: verbleibende Menge)

data.gloss: trans. durch Einkochen vermindern, konzentrieren (mit ʕal-: verbleibende Menge)

rationale: Single clear transitive/intransitive pairing: people reduce the juice, then it has reduced to half. The attested causative form supports provisional III; no unattested Preterit is supplied.

summary: New stem III ([Preterit unbelegt]/makət (aus kmakətənne erschlossen))

data.turoyo: W am maye di ḥalyuṯaṯe d ubʕi d saymila, kmakətənne ʕal falgayye
data.translation: Wenn man aus diesem Saft eine (andere) Süßigkeit herstellen will, kocht man (den Traubensaft) nur bis zur Hälfte ein.

rationale: New III stem and Infectum box; patient juice and endpoint are both explicit.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (JTM 1.1/52)

data.turoyo: bəṯr məd kayiti ʕal falgayye, kmanṭən qamḥo, howe naʕimo ste kowe, howe xašuno ste kowe. W kxulṭile b ḥḏoḏe, kowe ḥawdal
data.translation: Wenn er bis zur Hälfte eingekocht ist, holt man Mehl – es geht mit feinem, aber auch mit grobem Mehl – und mischt alles zusammen, dann ergibt das ḥawdal (Brei aus Trauben- saft).

rationale: Thin I Preterit Intransitive cell: liquid volume decreases, matching inherited 'to become less'.

summary: The source provides an unusually informative causative pairing: kmakətənne has a juice patient, while kayiti has the reduced juice as subject. ʕal falgayye marks the remaining quantity in both clauses.
Only III Infectum is attested here. Its base is inferred from kmakətənne; no unattested III Preterit or Imperativ is reconstructed.

Read-only kwt lookup found II Detransitive mikawət 'halb gekocht werden' with the same syrup domain, but no makət search hit. Semantic overlap does not by itself prove that kyt and kwt should be merged.
Confirm kyt III makət versus a contracted kwt-family form; compare the same-verse I kayiti and kwt II mikawət.
What is the III Preterit base? It is absent from this evidence and intentionally left unattested.
Does ʕal falgayye always name the remaining amount rather than an amount removed?
A liquid quantity becomes less through reduction to half; the inherited parenthesis 'to become less' covers this beyond the stunted-growth example.
